label: prop:hopf-link-symmetric-decomposition
title: Hopf-link symmetric decomposition: $\sigma_1^2 = q^2 e_+ + q^{-2} e_-$
html:
The Hopf element \sigma_1^2 of H_2(q) formally weights the two blocks by their squared eigenvalues:

  \sigma_1^2 = q^2 e_+ + q^{-2} e_-.

Equivalently, cleared of the [2]_q = q+q^{-1} denominator:

  [2]_q \sigma_1^2 = q^2 (\sigma_1+q^{-1}) + q^{-2} (q-\sigma_1).

This formally derives from the Hecke relation \sigma_1^2 = (q-q^{-1})\sigma_1 + 1.

The Hopf element \sigma_1^2 strictly splits between the symmetric e_+ and antisymmetric e_- blocks. At q_0, the symmetric weight fraction is q^2/(q^2+q^{-2}) \approx 60\;\text{\%}\%. This split fails to dominate. The van der Waals force avoids corresponding to the e_+ block. It identically corresponds to the bar-odd residual \sinh(2\lambda)(e_+-e_-) that the canonical P_{\mathrm{avg}} projection discards. The symmetric block e_+ acts strictly as the retained \cosh carrier, wholly distinct from the antisymmetric block e_-. Neither block alone constitutes van der Waals.

This establishes the formal structural identification. The molecular dispersion energy scale poses a separate archimedean (inter-molecular-separation) question. The bare e_+ resides at the \hbar_q-scale. This Hecke decomposition refuses to arbitrarily fix the long-distance suppression to the \sim 0.5\,\mathrm{kJ/mol} molecular van der Waals energy.
